boundary.note: The pre-DRAM path ends at the call of 0xb40690b8 (cold DRAM init wrapper) from 0xb4066718. The DRAM routine itself is out of scope (PR #4/#6).

established_by_firmware: Block 0 and main execute in A32 (ARM) state: every analysed instruction decodes as A32 and no BX/BLX to an odd address occurs on the path (decoded).
main clears the loader globals 0xb4070800..0xb407087b (memset, 0xb406540c) before anything else (decoded).
main reloads bootloader.ini (8 sectors) to 0xb4062400 through the Boot ROM service (decoded, executed).

No CP15 instruction runs before DRAM init: SCTLR is read and written (bit 12, I-cache) only by 0xb4065fc0/0xb4065fdc, which main calls after dram_caller returns or on its ADFU exit; VBAR is written (0xffff0000) only in rom_reentry_adfu 0xb406921c (decoded).
No instruction on the pre-DRAM path writes SP, CPSR or SPSR; no MMU, D-cache or cache maintenance operation exists in the reachable code (decoded).
inherited_from_boot_rom: Stack pointer: neither block 0 nor main sets SP; the value is the Boot ROM's (unknown). The emulator uses 0xb409f000; the deepest pre-DRAM stack use measured there is 136 bytes.

CPU mode, interrupt masks, exception vector base and SCTLR (MMU/caches) at entry: not set before DRAM init, so inherited (unknown). The emulator starts in SVC mode with IRQ/FIQ masked (0x1d3) - an emulator choice.

SRAM mapping 0xb4060000.. with block 0 at 0xb4060000; the Boot ROM service entry 0xb4060400 and the code at 0xb4060758 live in the zero hole 0x400..0x1e00 of the image, so they are placed there by the ROM.
Clock tree: HOSC (24 MHz by the delay constant 24 ticks/us and the UART formula 24000000/(8*baud)) and bus clocks are not programmed before DRAM init except the gates/resets listed in the inventory.
CMU_DEVCLKEN0 bit 7 (SD2 gate in the related S500 tree) - read by block 0, set by the ROM (inferred).
supplied_by_emulator: T0 count word (timer base+8, 0xb0168010): +24 per read (1 synthetic us per read)
UART status (base+0xc): 0x400 (bit 10 set, bit 6 clear) - TX never full, always drains
I2C base+0x20: 0x1 (bit 0 set, bit 1 clear) - every probe/transfer completes without error
GPIO C data (0xb01b0020): last written value; bit 10 := 0 (no-loopback) or := bit 11 (loopback)
any other MMIO read: last value written there, else the run seed (0 or 0xffffffff)
PMIC I2C transactions (0xb406ac10 read / 0xb406ac60 write) served by a register file (Pmic)
Boot ROM service r9=4 (sector read) served from the disk image
SRAM 0xb4060000..0xb4093c00 := loader bytes from the image (the ROM-filled hole stays zero)
boot code word 0xb4064c00 := 0 or 2 (as block 0 would write)
inferred: The loader expects SRAM to persist between block 0 and main (shared 0xb4064c00 word, AFI at 0xb4060300) and to be at least 0xb4070880 long (globals).
unknown: Boot ROM register state at the jump to 0xb4060000 (r0-r12, lr)
whether L2 / caches were left enabled by the ROM

block0.note: No instruction in block 0 writes SP, CPSR or CP15; calls to 0xb4060400 (r9 selector) and to addresses in the zero hole are Boot ROM code that the image does not contain.

writers.note: Codes 0 and 2 then share one instruction path: ROM service r9=4, sector 0x102b, 0x50 sectors to 0xb4065400, blx 0xb4065400. 0xb01600a0 is CMU_DEVCLKEN0 in the related S500 clock tree; which Boot ROM search sets bit 7 is inferred (BOOT-012), not observed.

references.note: 0xb4064000 is also the base other code uses for 0xb4064c60..c74 (publish_globals); a literal is a data word, not evidence of a use. Uses are the decoded loads/stores and calls above.

status_bit_test.meaning: bit 1 set -> write back with bits 0-1 cleared, then ADFU

status_clear.meaning: value written back to the status register

enable_argument.meaning: r0 at entry = ini word +0x14; 0 -> return

boot_code_test.meaning: get_boot_code(); 0 -> return (SD0 path skips the GPIO test)

drive_bit.meaning: GPIO C data bit 11 := next pattern bit

sample_bit.meaning: GPIO C data bit 10 sampled after the delay

success_compare.meaning: sampled word == pattern -> print "Prepare to entry ADFU mode", tail-call 0xb40691a4

adfu_check.names: C10/C11 follow the related-SoC GPIO bank layout (A at 0x00, B 0x0c, C 0x18: OUTEN, INEN, DAT); the physical pins are not established.

wrap_safe_compare.meaning: loop while (int32)(now - target) < 0: wrap-safe, unbounded if the count never advances

tx_empty_poll.meaning: then wait until status bit 10 set (unbounded)

handle.meaning: table entry pointer -> 0xb4070800 (0 when no entry matches)

dram_stage_code0_vs_code2.note: The other PR #6 training/failure scenarios were not re-run for code 2 (out of scope). The harness answers GPIO reads with the last value written, i.e. it models "no loopback".

unresolved_static_accesses.note: Loads/stores whose base register is not a block-local constant (pointer arguments, globals reached through registers). Those on the executed path are attributed in register_inventory from the trace; the rest are not resolved.

release_comparison.normalisation: None. Hashes are of the raw instruction words each function decodes (code_sha256) and of the raw bytes from entry to the end of its literal pool (extent_sha256). Event sequences compare (op, address, value, function) after collapsing consecutive identical events into one entry with a count; instruction counts are not compared.

synthetic_rules.i2c_fifostat: I2C base+0x20: 0x1 (bit 0 set, bit 1 clear) - every probe/transfer completes without error

emulation_audit.detail: boot code is a parameter (0 and 2 used by boot-path); stubs timer_init, uart_init, board_mfp_init, pmu_init, adfu_check and the DRAM init with return 0, so none of the code-dependent pre-DRAM behaviour executes there.
boot_code defaults to 0; run_caller() never passes it, so every committed DRAM-stage run used code 0 and skipped the GPIO handshake.
uart_init 0xb4066784 and pmu_detect 0xb4069890 are stubbed; delay 0xb40693f8 and printf are stubbed by ddr_emulate; PMIC accessors 0xb4069610/0xb40696c0 are a register file.

non-DDR MMIO reads return the last written value or a reset seed, so GPIO C data reads in the handshake would return what was written (bit 10 never mirrors bit 11) - that silently models "no loopback".
starts at 0xb4065ff8 or the DRAM routine; nothing before the ini copy is executed.

executes main from 0xb4065400 through every pre-DRAM function including timer, UART, board, PMIC detection/bus selection and the ADFU check; stubs only printf, the Boot ROM read service and the I2C transaction layer (0xb406ac10/0xb406ac60). Reads follow SYNTHETIC_RULES; stops at 0xb40690b8.

unknowns: Electrical meaning of every PMIC write (no PMIC datasheet for the type-2 device; the vendor kernel driver names are not established for this board).
Real reset values of the MFP/CMU/GPIO registers the pre-DRAM code read-modify-writes (seeded reads).
Whether GPIO C10/C11 are connected to anything on the RG35XX board, so whether the code-2 loopback test can ever succeed on a production unit.
Pin assignment of UART3 pad 0: its table entry performs no pin-mux write, so the console pins rely on register state set elsewhere (ROM or reset default) - not established.
Real elapsed time of the delays (depends on the timer clock actually being 24 MHz).
Whether the Boot ROM leaves the I2C/UART/timer blocks clocked; the loader enables the gates itself.
